consolidated_resolution_slate.title: Closed authority-anchor variants
consolidated_resolution_slate.question: Which exact three-variant anchor representation governs generation naming, genesis predecessor nullability, and RESTORE_INTENT coordinates?

options.label: D0-first proposed-coordinate variants
options.rule: Use a closed oneOf for MUTATION_INTENT, RESTORE_INTENT, and COMMITTED; name the generation field last_generation; use null for the bootstrap-genesis predecessor_anchor_digest; make intent top-level instance, restore_epoch, last_generation, global_event_seq, global_event_head_digest, and database_header_digest the proposed committed coordinates while retaining explicit old_event_head_digest and proposed_next_event_head_digest plus the candidate and expected committed digests. COMMITTED requires intent-only fields to be null and predecessor_anchor_digest to be non-null except at bootstrap genesis.

consequences.security: The intent is a complete candidate-anchor projection, the old/proposed head pair remains explicit, and anchor genesis cannot be confused with the event-chain empty predecessor.
consequences.compatibility: Renames accepted authority_generation to last_generation in the owner-only external anchor schema; no public MCP tool or result changes.
consequences.counts: 16 tables, 32 operations, 24 owner operations, 53 errors, 34 pack leaves, and 67 MCP vectors remain unchanged.
consequences.schema: audit-receipt.schema.json authority_anchor becomes a three-branch additionalProperties:false oneOf with equality and nullability constraints.
consequences.vectors: Add every old/new/intent crash pairing, genesis-null, predecessor mismatch, fork, alias, and multi-drift negative.

options.label: Accepted-name old-coordinate intents
options.rule: Keep authority_generation, use the event empty-string digest for bootstrap predecessor_anchor_digest, and make RESTORE_INTENT top-level coordinates the old authority while carrying proposed values only in candidate fields.

consequences.security: Can be made closed, but conflates two independent genesis domains and makes the intent less directly comparable to the candidate committed anchor.
consequences.compatibility: Preserves one accepted field name but changes its meaning by variant and retains more accepted-shape familiarity.
consequences.schema: Still requires a three-branch oneOf and explicit candidate fields.
consequences.vectors: Requires separate old-coordinate versus candidate-coordinate equality vectors.

options.label: Flat nullable superset
options.rule: Keep one closed object with nullable fields and no state-specific oneOf.

consequences.security: Allows semantically incomplete or hybrid intent/committed combinations unless correctness is deferred to runtime; this is not an adequate closed contract.
consequences.compatibility: Smallest structural edit to accepted F1 but preserves the class of underbinding that caused the stop.
consequences.schema: Adds properties without discriminated branch exclusion.
consequences.vectors: Cannot express schema-level rejection of cross-variant fields.

recommendation.rationale: It follows the ratified anchor.last_generation spelling and three-durable-point recovery intent, while keeping event genesis and anchor genesis distinct.
recommendation.exact_variant_rule: All listed fields are required, including nullable fields. Intent branches require non-null candidate_event_digest, candidate_database_digest, expected_committed_anchor_digest, old_event_head_digest, proposed_next_event_head_digest, and predecessor_anchor_digest. COMMITTED requires those five intent-only fields to be null, requires predecessor_anchor_digest except at bootstrap genesis, and uses null only for that bootstrap-genesis predecessor. RESTORE_INTENT top-level authority and event coordinates are the proposed committed coordinates.

consolidated_resolution_slate.title: Restore publication aggregates and global head
consolidated_resolution_slate.question: Which exact invalidation aggregates and head fields prove that restore published a complete replacement rather than a hybrid authority?

options.label: Six disjoint aggregates; event digest is head
options.rule: Require exactly revoked_credential_count plus revoked_credentials_digest, closed_session_count plus closed_sessions_digest, invalidated_request_count plus invalidated_requests_digest, invalidated_cursor_count plus invalidated_cursors_digest, invalidated_snapshot_count plus invalidated_snapshots_digest, and invalidated_idempotency_record_count plus invalidated_idempotency_records_digest as six disjoint count plus ordered-set-digest pairs; also require restored_database_digest. Treat event-common global_event_seq and event_digest as the new global sequence and head, with no duplicate new_global_event_head_digest field.

consequences.security: Each durable invalidation class is independently auditable; a hybrid restore cannot hide behind one opaque aggregate; duplicate head fields cannot disagree.
consequences.compatibility: Adds owner-only restore-event fields and replaces accepted generic booleans/digests; public MCP is unchanged.
consequences.counts: The restore_events table remains table 16; no operation, owner-operation, error, leaf, or MCP count changes.
consequences.schema: authority_restore becomes a closed branch requiring the six count/digest pairs, old/new authority coordinates, replacement-owner binding, restored_database_digest, and publication constants.
consequences.vectors: RESTORE-OWNER vectors must assert each count, ordered digest, database digest, global_event_seq, and event_digest.

options.label: One combined invalidation aggregate
options.rule: Use one invalidated_state_count and invalidated_state_digest across requests, cursors, snapshots, and idempotency while keeping credentials and sessions separate.

consequences.security: Proves a combined set but cannot independently verify that every required state class was covered.
consequences.compatibility: Smaller schema expansion than A.
consequences.schema: Fewer fields but weaker class closure.
consequences.vectors: Would need opaque aggregate reconstruction tooling and cannot isolate an omitted class.

options.label: Six aggregates plus duplicate new head
options.rule: Use option A and add new_global_event_head_digest constrained equal to event_digest.

consequences.security: Equivalent only if equality is enforced; otherwise creates a forkable duplicate claim.
consequences.compatibility: Adds one redundant field to every restore receipt.
consequences.schema: Requires a non-native cross-field equality assertion in generation/runtime checks.
consequences.vectors: Adds mismatch-negative cases without adding semantic evidence.

recommendation.rationale: It is the smallest partition that proves every D0 invalidation class, and event_digest already is the globally chained new head.

consolidated_resolution_slate.title: Restore plan, abort states, locator disposition, and generation
consolidated_resolution_slate.question: What exact external plan representation and prepublication abort protocol governs staged locator recovery?

options.label: Canonical relative locator; two-state abort
options.rule: Store a canonical relative temporary_locator_name beneath the fixed verified credential parent plus temporary_path_binding_digest, physical_identity_digest, content_digest, protection_digest, owner_digest, regular_file=true, and no_link=true; never store a raw absolute path. The external plan states are RESTORE_PLAN_STAGED, RESTORE_OWNER_LOCATOR_STAGED, RESTORE_INTENT, COMMITTED, RESTORE_ABORT_INTENT, and ABORTED. Abort is callable only from RESTORE_PLAN_STAGED or RESTORE_OWNER_LOCATOR_STAGED while database_publication_started=false and anchor_publication_started=false. Bind staged_locator_kind=temporary|final and staged_locator_disposition=deleted_exact|absent|preserved_unsafe. Abort keeps authority_instance_id and restore_epoch, advances authority_generation and the global event chain exactly once, stales all pre-plan sessions and admitted requests, invalidates all pre-plan cursors/snapshots, leaves old active credentials usable for fresh authentication, and tombstones the abandoned replacement credential and plan.

consequences.security: No raw path leaks; cleanup is identity-bound; both prepublication staged states have a reachable fail-closed escape; unsafe objects are preserved; reconnect requires fresh current authorization.
consequences.compatibility: Clarifies and modestly broadens abort from the prose's named RESTORE_PLAN_STAGED point to both prepublication states; no public MCP change.
consequences.counts: restore_plan and restore_abort_intent remain external $defs in an existing leaf; 16 tables, 32 operations, 24 owner operations, 53 errors, and 34 pack leaves remain exact.
consequences.schema: Add closed restore_plan and restore_abort_intent definitions; make restore abort result/receipt state-discriminated and replace temporary-only disposition with staged locator kind plus disposition.
consequences.vectors: Cover both abort source states, exact temp/final deletion, absence, unsafe preservation, generation plus one, session/request/cursor/snapshot invalidation, tombstone split crash, and rejection from RESTORE_INTENT or later.

options.label: Digest-derived name; plan-stage-only abort
options.rule: Derive the relative locator name from restore_plan_id and store only its path-binding digest; allow abort only in RESTORE_PLAN_STAGED; leave authority_generation and old sessions unchanged.

consequences.security: Avoids a stored name but leaves locator-staged failures with continuation as the only path and permits pre-plan sessions to survive a closed-gate security transition.
consequences.compatibility: Closer to the narrowest reading of the existing abort prose.
consequences.schema: Fewer locator fields and narrower state transition.
consequences.vectors: Requires permanent fail-closed cases for locator-staged plans that cannot continue.

options.label: Protected raw path; broad abort
options.rule: Persist a protected absolute path and allow abort from any non-COMMITTED plan state, including RESTORE_INTENT.

consequences.security: Leaks host-specific path material and permits rollback after publication has begun, conflicting with anchor recovery and fail-closed publication semantics.
consequences.compatibility: Creates host-specific backup/restore records.
consequences.schema: Requires raw path fields and ambiguous postpublication disposition.
consequences.vectors: Would need rollback cases that conflict with ratified no-guessed-repair rules.

recommendation.rationale: It gives every prepublication staged credential object an exact recover-or-tombstone path while retaining the old authority and forbidding rollback after RESTORE_INTENT.

consolidated_resolution_slate.title: Restore-plan discovery after an ambiguous response
consolidated_resolution_slate.question: How does the exact pre-restore owner recover a server-generated restore_plan_id without a new side channel?

options.label: Extend authority.status
options.rule: Keep authority.status OWNER_ONLY and add required nullable restore_recovery={restore_plan_id,state,state_digest,abort_eligible}. During write_gate=recovery_required|blocked, only owner_cli may call this read path after reauthentication of the exact pre-restore credential and equality with the active plan's old authority coordinates. The object forbids raw paths, credential material/digests, physical identity details, and protection descriptors.

consequences.security: Provides one authenticated nonsecret discovery path under a closed gate without weakening abort authentication.
consequences.compatibility: Changes only an owner-only result schema; public MCP tools, inputs, results, and catalog stay byte-semantically unchanged.
consequences.counts: Exactly 32 operations and 24 owner operations remain; authority.status remains nonmutating.
consequences.schema: operation-inventory authority_status_result gains one closed nullable object and recovery-gate transport rules.
consequences.vectors: RESTORE-STATUS-DISCOVERY-001 proves lost response, one active plan, exact ID/digest, redaction, and successful abort.

options.label: Add restore-plan inspect
options.rule: Add owner-only authority.restore.inspect with a dedicated result.

consequences.security: Can be made safe but introduces a second recovery read surface.
consequences.compatibility: Requires inventory, schema, docs, fixture, and evidence count changes; still no public MCP tool if kept owner-only.
consequences.counts: Operations become 33 and owner-only operations become 25.
consequences.schema: Adds request/result definitions and an inventory entry.
consequences.vectors: Every exact-count and unknown-operation vector must change.

options.label: Client-chosen plan identifier
options.rule: Make restore_plan_id caller-supplied before staging and remove server-side discovery.

consequences.security: Avoids discovery but moves identifier collision and binding responsibility to an authenticated client and changes idempotency semantics.
consequences.compatibility: Changes authority.restore request semantics.
consequences.schema: Adds restore_plan_id to the request and collision rules.
consequences.vectors: Requires caller-ID collision, replay, and cross-owner binding cases.

recommendation.rationale: It is the only choice that preserves the ratified exact operation counts and adds no new authority or public MCP surface.

consolidated_resolution_slate.title: Bootstrap vocabulary and pre-authority crash recovery
consolidated_resolution_slate.derived_part: The state vocabulary is already ratified and is not a free owner choice: UNINITIALIZED, OWNER_PROVED, PLAN_STAGED, OWNER_LOCATOR_STAGED, DB_COMMITTED, ANCHOR_COMMITTED, OWNER_ACTIVE, LEGACY_ACTIVE, LEGACY_REVOKED, COMPLETE, and BLOCKED with the two exact terminal branches.
consolidated_resolution_slate.question: How is the secret-loss window between owner proof and a durable bootstrap plan made recoverable without an authenticated authority?

options.label: Temp-before-plan
options.rule: Persist the closed OWNER_PROVED external record, create/fsync an implementation-owned protected credential temporary, then atomically persist PLAN_STAGED binding that exact temp before renaming it to the default locator and advancing to OWNER_LOCATOR_STAGED. A crash before the plan rename may remove only the exact verified unreferenced temp and retry from OWNER_PROVED with fresh IDs/secret; after PLAN_STAGED, recovery must reuse the bound temp and never regenerate or re-reveal. Use only the ratified vocabulary and remove DB_PUBLISHED, LEGACY_REMOVED, and RECOVERY_REQUIRED as states.

consequences.security: Eliminates the unauthenticated blocked-plan deadlock without creating repeat OS-owner administration authority; referenced secrets are never discarded or regenerated.
consequences.compatibility: Amends bootstrap staging order but preserves all durable state names, one-time locator handoff, and local-bootstrap-only authority.
consequences.counts: 16 tables and the existing one LOCAL_BOOTSTRAP operation remain; no new operation or error code.
consequences.schema: bootstrap-migration.schema.json gains closed external owner-proof/plan variants and exact state transitions; authority_meta.bootstrap_state is closed.
consequences.vectors: Add BOOTSTRAP-PLAN-CRASH-001 for pre-plan cleanup/retry and retain BOOTSTRAP-LOCATOR-ROLLBACK-001 for post-plan exact reuse.

options.label: Fresh OS-owner recovery variant
options.rule: Keep plan-before-temp ordering and add a fresh interactive OS-owner-proof bootstrap.initialize recovery/abort variant that tombstones a blocked abandoned plan before generating new IDs or secret.

consequences.security: Can recover, but creates a second pre-authority mutation authority and requires exact anti-replay/challenge/tombstone rules.
consequences.compatibility: Expands bootstrap.initialize semantics while preserving operation count.
consequences.counts: Counts stay unchanged if represented as a request variant; schema definition/vector counts grow.
consequences.schema: Adds a recovery discriminator and blocked-plan tombstone evidence.
consequences.vectors: Requires proof freshness, abandoned-plan collision, double recovery, and crash-at-tombstone cases.

options.label: Authenticated migration.recover
options.rule: Leave ordering unchanged and require OWNER_ONLY migration.recover after a pre-authority crash.

consequences.security: Unreachable because no active credential or authority exists; the vault remains permanently blocked.
consequences.compatibility: No schema expansion but an unusable recovery promise.
consequences.schema: Retains the contradiction.
consequences.vectors: Cannot produce a successful pre-authority recovery vector.

recommendation.rationale: It closes the crash window with the smallest semantic amendment and no new authority, operation, state name, or error.

consolidated_resolution_slate.title: Core and recovery vector accounting
consolidated_resolution_slate.question: How are the ratified eight core-operation vectors and ten separately frozen restore/bootstrap recovery vectors counted?

options.label: Separate 8 plus 10 classes
options.rule: Keep f1_core_operation_vector_count=8 for BOOTSTRAP-SOURCE-001..004 and CREDENTIAL-RESULT-001..004; add f1_restore_bootstrap_recovery_vector_count=10 for RESTORE-OWNER-001..009 and BOOTSTRAP-LOCATOR-ROLLBACK-001; state combined_required_non_mcp_core_vectors=18. Keep official_mcp_vectors=67 and attach aliases rather than renumbering the 67 IDs.

consequences.security: All mandatory crash/recovery cases become executable without erasing the meaning of the existing eight-vector class.
consequences.compatibility: Preserves ratified IDs and public MCP vector coordinates.
consequences.counts: 8 core-operation plus 10 recovery equals 18 combined; MCP remains 67.
consequences.schema: Decision record and conformance metadata gain explicit class counts.
consequences.vectors: Adds the missing ten as closed scenario vectors and core_vector_id aliases for existing semantic MCP cases.

options.label: Single total of 18
options.rule: Rename the existing field to f1_core_operation_vector_count=18 and place all cases in one class.

consequences.security: Covers all cases but loses the ratified distinction between operation and recovery vectors.
consequences.compatibility: Changes an accepted decision/count meaning.
consequences.schema: Simpler count field but requires amendments to every eight-count assertion.
consequences.vectors: IDs may remain unchanged.

options.label: Keep only eight
options.rule: Treat the ten named recovery vectors as prose and preserve the existing fixture count.

consequences.security: Leaves the stopped restore/bootstrap crash protocol unqualified.
consequences.compatibility: Preserves accepted F1 but contradicts ratified D0.
consequences.schema: No correction.
consequences.vectors: Ten required vectors remain absent.

recommendation.rationale: This is directly implied by the decision record's named eight-vector class and D0-6's separately named ten-vector recovery family; no discrete owner choice is needed unless D0 semantics are intentionally amended.

consolidated_resolution_slate.title: Durable page-snapshot bytes and cursor restart
consolidated_resolution_slate.question: Does a page snapshot persist its authorized payload and remain usable after process restart during its 15-minute life?

options.label: Persist canonical payload; survive restart
options.rule: Replace integer canonical_bytes with canonical_byte_length 0..524288 and canonical_payload_base64url containing the exact canonical UTF-8 authorized redacted summary bytes, with strict decode-length equality and byte-identical re-encode. Add policy_decision_id, nullable scope_ref_digest, nullable physical_identity_digest, nullable temporal_at, nullable temporal_state=valid|superseded|not_yet_created|all|null, and authorization_binding_digest. Compute authorization_binding_digest as SHA-256 over domain GKOS-PAGE-SNAPSHOT-AUTHORIZATION-V1, NUL, and canonical JSON of vault/authority/restore/generation, agent/auth epoch/session/transport/operation, policy decision, scope/physical/filter/temporal/order, snapshot digest, and expiry. Page cursors repeat policy_decision_id and authorization_binding_digest and require equality with the referenced row. An unexpired valid cursor resumes from SQLite after restart.

consequences.security: Restart cannot substitute process-memory pages or weaken the graph authorization tuple; only already-authorized redacted bytes persist.
consequences.compatibility: Corrects an accepted field type and strengthens owner/private storage; public page semantics remain the ratified stable-snapshot behavior.
consequences.counts: The existing page_snapshots and page_cursors tables remain tables 13 and 14; 32/24 operations and public MCP tool counts do not change.
consequences.schema: audit-receipt page_snapshot/page_cursor definitions gain payload and binding fields with strict base64url validation.
consequences.vectors: SNAPSHOT-RESTART-001 proves continuation from SQLite only; add binding mismatch, canonical alias, length mismatch, expiry, and restore-invalidation negatives.

options.label: Invalidate cursors on restart
options.rule: Keep only snapshot digest/count metadata and define every process restart as cursor invalidation.

consequences.security: Fail-closed but weakens the ratified durable row and 15-minute stable-snapshot semantics.
consequences.compatibility: Introduces a visible restart-dependent cursor failure.
consequences.schema: No payload field; requires explicit process epoch binding.
consequences.vectors: Restart must always yield the closed invalid-cursor projection.

options.label: Process-memory snapshot cache
options.rule: Persist only counts/digests and reconstruct pages from a process-local cache when present.

consequences.security: Produces nondurable behavior and cannot prove the stored snapshot digest corresponds to returned bytes after restart.
consequences.compatibility: Matches the stopped draft's behavior only.
consequences.schema: Remains underbound.
consequences.vectors: Cannot pass restart qualification.

recommendation.rationale: D0 says snapshots materialize bounded bytes, persist as rows until receipted expiry, and bind cursors; restart invalidation would be a semantic amendment rather than a correction.

consolidated_resolution_slate.title: Global event kind-to-table constants
consolidated_resolution_slate.question: Which exact event_kind spellings close the four event tables?

options.label: Singular record-kind constants
options.rule: Freeze identity_audit_receipt for identity_audit_receipts, retention_batch for retention_batches, effect_outbox_event for effect_outbox_events, and restore_event for restore_events.

consequences.security: Startup can reject kind/table aliases, cross-table substitution, and duplicate union entries with exact constants.
consequences.compatibility: Adds exact enum values where accepted F1 allowed arbitrary strings; no public MCP change.
consequences.counts: Four event kinds across the existing four event tables; no table, operation, error, leaf, or MCP count change.
consequences.schema: Each event definition uses a table-specific const and the global union dispatches on those values.
consequences.vectors: Add every wrong-table kind, case/Unicode alias, cross-table duplicate ID/sequence, gap, fork, genesis, and restore-floor negative.

options.label: Plural SQL-table constants
options.rule: Use identity_audit_receipts, retention_batches, effect_outbox_events, and restore_events.

consequences.security: Equivalent closure if exact.
consequences.compatibility: Couples the canonical event wire to plural physical table names.
consequences.schema: Four alternate consts.
consequences.vectors: Same coverage with plural expected bytes.

recommendation.rationale: The singular values match the ratified record names and the contract-steward correction without exposing physical SQL naming as wire semantics.

consolidated_resolution_slate.title: Race final gate after global generation drift
consolidated_resolution_slate.question: Does an unrelated agent mutation automatically stale otherwise valid work?

options.label: Selective bound-principal revalidation
options.rule: At the read-result gate or immediately before the first irreversible effect commit under A-to-E, reread current instance/restore/generation/write gate, affected agent status and auth_epoch, credential status/ownership, session state/expiry, policy/configuration and required capability/dependency bindings, and scope/physical bindings. If only authority_generation changed and every affected binding remains equal, permit publication and record the current authority_generation_final. If any affected binding changed, persist request state stale, publish no result/effect/success activity, and return GKOS_P6_REQUEST_STALE_AUTHORITY.

consequences.security: No stale allow survives; unrelated agents cannot cause denial-of-service by generation churn.
consequences.compatibility: Exactly matches ratified D0 lines 1019-1025 and requires the missing request stale state.
consequences.counts: No count change and no public MCP schema change beyond already-ratified error behavior.
consequences.schema: request state adds stale; final coordinates remain explicit.
consequences.vectors: Cover same-agent and different-agent generation changes before/after final gate, reconnect, cancellation, effect commit, restart, and multiprocess order.

options.label: Unconditional generation equality
options.rule: Any authority_generation change stales the request without rereading affected bindings.

consequences.security: Safe but creates cross-agent denial-of-service and contradicts the ratified selective rule.
consequences.compatibility: Changes deterministic race outcomes.
consequences.schema: Simpler runtime predicate only.
consequences.vectors: Different-agent mutation must stale, contrary to D0.

options.label: Ignore generation drift
options.rule: Check only the admission snapshot and do no final revalidation.

consequences.security: Allows revoked, disabled, stale-policy, or recovery-blocked work to publish.
consequences.compatibility: Violates the final-gate contract.
consequences.schema: Leaves stale state unused.
consequences.vectors: Fails lifecycle-race negatives.

recommendation.rationale: The ratified text resolves this deterministically; owner action is needed only to reject and amend that rule.

consolidated_resolution_slate.title: Credential issuance epoch and continuing authentication
consolidated_resolution_slate.question: Does issuing one credential silently invalidate other status=active credentials?

options.label: Historical issuance coordinate
options.rule: credential.issue increments global authority_generation and the affected agent auth_epoch exactly once, stales all earlier sessions and admitted work for that agent, and writes the new credential's auth_epoch_issued as the new epoch. Continuing authentication requires the credential status active and the current agent active; it does not require auth_epoch_issued=current auth_epoch. Every other active credential remains usable for a fresh session at the current epoch. revoke and rotate affect only the selected credential, with rotate inserting one new active credential and revoking the selected old one.

consequences.security: All old work is stale while multiple independently attributable active credentials remain intentional and auditable.
consequences.compatibility: Matches the ratified four-active-credentials limit and issuance-coordinate schema; removes the stopped draft's accidental implicit revocation.
consequences.counts: No count, public MCP, table, or error change.
consequences.schema: Clarify auth_epoch_issued as immutable history and close active/revoked credential nullability; no new field is required.
consequences.vectors: Prove prior active credential reconnect after issue, all old sessions stale, selected-only revoke/rotate, and no equality gate.

options.label: Epoch equality authentication
options.rule: Require every credential auth_epoch_issued to equal the current agent epoch.

consequences.security: Silently disables every prior active credential whenever any lifecycle mutation increments the epoch.
consequences.compatibility: Contradicts multiple active credentials and status history.
consequences.schema: Makes active status misleading.
consequences.vectors: Prior-active reconnect must fail.

options.label: Issue does not advance epoch
options.rule: Keep prior sessions and work live when credential.issue commits.

consequences.security: Weakens the ratified stale-work boundary for a security-relevant credential mutation.
consequences.compatibility: Contradicts D0's exact increment rule.
consequences.schema: No schema expansion.
consequences.vectors: Issue-before-final-gate work would remain valid contrary to D0.

recommendation.rationale: This is the only interpretation consistent with both epoch-based stale work and up to four active credentials per agent.

consolidated_resolution_slate.title: Sole-owner rotation after lost postcommit handoff
consolidated_resolution_slate.question: What prevents permanent owner lockout when rotation revokes the sole usable credential before a new one-time handoff is lost?

options.label: Require a second handed-off owner credential
options.rule: Before credential.rotate may target an owner_admin credential, require at least one other distinct status=active owner_admin credential for the same owner agent with durable successful handoff evidence. If absent, return GKOS_P6_STATE_CONFLICT with zero mutation, zero new credential, and zero handoff. The owner first uses credential.issue; a lost issue handoff leaves the old credential active, and a lost rotate handoff leaves the second credential usable.

consequences.security: Preserves zero grace, no re-reveal, no OS-owner repeat administration, and no new recovery authority while preventing sole-credential lockout.
consequences.compatibility: Adds a precondition to owner credential rotation; issue remains the safe enrollment path.
consequences.counts: No operation, owner-operation, error, table, leaf, or public MCP count change; active credential cap remains four.
consequences.schema: Credential handoff evidence must distinguish committed, delivered, and failed delivery without storing secret/path content.
consequences.vectors: Cover sole-credential rejection, issue failure with old credential retained, two-credential rotation success, lost rotate handoff, replay false, and recovery through the second credential.

options.label: Independent recovery authority
options.rule: Allow sole-owner rotation and define a separate authenticated recovery principal capable of rotating after lockout.

consequences.security: Adds a high-value authority and credential lifecycle that must be protected, revoked, audited, and recovered.
consequences.compatibility: Expands the authority model and likely operation/request schemas.
consequences.counts: Could preserve counts only by overloading an existing operation; a clean design likely changes operation or authority counts.
consequences.schema: Requires recovery-principal, proof, policy, and event records.
consequences.vectors: Requires full recovery credential non-enumeration, rotation, revocation, compromise, and race coverage.

options.label: Version sequencing or grace
options.rule: Change rotation so old revocation follows successful handoff or introduce a grace window.

consequences.security: Avoids lockout but abandons zero grace and changes the deterministic race boundary.
consequences.compatibility: Requires a new protocol version and revised rotation results.
consequences.counts: Counts may remain but contract version and many vectors change.
consequences.schema: Adds pending/grace states and timing fields.
consequences.vectors: Requires dual-active, crash, replay, timeout, and revoke-during-grace cases.

recommendation.rationale: It resolves the contradiction using already-ratified multiple active credentials and does not add authority or weaken zero grace.

consolidated_resolution_slate.title: External mapping availability before adapter authentication
consolidated_resolution_slate.question: May mapping.add or mapping.revoke bind an owner-supplied external subject before a qualified authenticated adapter exists?

options.label: Inventory-present but unavailable
options.rule: Keep mapping.add and mapping.revoke in the exact owner-only inventory but return GKOS_P6_PLATFORM_UNAVAILABLE with zero mutation until a separately ratified adapter authenticates a stable namespace and canonical subject. The eventual request carries a nonsecret authenticated adapter evidence/reference, not a raw owner-supplied external_subject; authenticated_by is a closed adapter identifier/evidence digest, not a free string.

consequences.security: Prevents owners or callers from forging external identity bindings and stores no raw subject.
consequences.compatibility: The operations remain discoverable in owner inventory but fail closed until dependency qualification; no public MCP tool exists for them.
consequences.counts: Exactly 32 operations and 24 owner operations remain; error count stays 53.

consolidated_resolution_slate.title: Prospective retention policy, history, and source sequences
consolidated_resolution_slate.question: What does prospective mean, and how is the applied policy reconstructible without a seventeenth table?

options.label: Creation-time policy binding in 16 tables
options.rule: Store current retention_days 7..365, retention_effective_from, and retention_policy_digest in authority_meta, initialized to 90 and authority creation time. A set_retention receipt permanently stores exact before/after days, effective times, and policy digests. The new value applies only to purgeable rows created at or after retention_effective_from; each closed session, request, policy decision, and activity binds retention_policy_digest_at_creation. Add monotonic retention_sequence to session, request, and policy-decision rows; activity_seq serves activity. Each retention_batch names one record_type, the exact policy digest applied, true inclusive first/last source sequences, row count, ordered row digest, and deletion time. Sweeps delete only complete UTC days, respect the 24-hour idempotency minimum and active-row protection, and use the normal mutation-intent/event transaction.

consequences.security: No retroactive shortening, fabricated sequence evidence, or policy-history loss; every deletion is reconstructible.
consequences.compatibility: Adds fields to existing records and a closed set_retention receipt variant; retention.get/set operation semantics stay owner-only.
consequences.counts: Exactly 16 tables, 32 operations, 24 owner operations, and 53 errors remain; no new pack leaf or public MCP change.
consequences.schema: authority_meta, the four purgeable record classes, identity audit set_retention, and retention_batch gain exact policy/sequence fields.
consequences.vectors: Cover set/restart/get, multiple policy versions, old/new row eligibility, complete UTC-day boundaries, true sequences/digests, authorization, restore preservation, 24-hour replay, crash, and active-row denial.

options.label: Current policy governs every future sweep
options.rule: A new retention value applies to all rows whenever a later sweep runs, including rows created before retention_effective_from; store only current policy plus setting receipts.

consequences.security: A shorter new value can retroactively accelerate deletion and a longer value can retain older rows unexpectedly.
consequences.compatibility: Simpler row schema but changes the literal prospective meaning.
consequences.schema: Source sequences are still required for truthful batch evidence, but per-row policy binding is absent.
consequences.vectors: Must prove retroactive sweep behavior explicitly.

options.label: Dedicated retention-policy table
options.rule: Create a seventeenth table for current and historical retention versions and foreign-key purgeable rows to it.

consequences.security: Can be reconstructible, but introduces a new normalized state surface.
consequences.compatibility: Contradicts the exact 16-table D0 model and changes backup/restore/startup schemas.
consequences.schema: Adds a table, migrations, FKs, manifest expectations, and restoration rules.
consequences.vectors: All schema/table-count and backup/restore fixtures must change.

recommendation.rationale: It gives prospective its literal non-retroactive meaning, makes policy selection and purge evidence permanent, and preserves the exact 16-table design.

consolidated_resolution_slate.title: Closed activity metadata value domains
consolidated_resolution_slate.question: Which non-content value domains are allowed under the six base activity metadata keys?

options.label: Typed integers and closed enums
options.rule: input_bytes, output_bytes, item_count, and result_count are nonnegative safe integers. cache_outcome is exactly not_applicable|hit|miss|bypassed. side_effect_class is exactly read|compute_only|proposal_only|authority_mutation|qualified_external_effect. Keys remain optional, at most 16 total and 8192 canonical bytes, and operation-specific schemas may remove values but not add free strings.

consequences.security: Paths, subjects, SQL, stack, credentials, and user content cannot be smuggled through metadata strings.
consequences.compatibility: The three public-tool side-effect values remain aligned with the ratified MCP catalog; owner/effect activity gains two closed values.
consequences.counts: No count change and no MCP tool/catalog semantic change.
consequences.schema: activity.schema.json applies per-key types/enums and additionalProperties:false to metadata.
consequences.vectors: Accept every enum/integer boundary; reject arbitrary strings, negative/fractional/unsafe integers, content-bearing attempts, and unknown keys.

options.label: Remove categorical keys
options.rule: Allow only the four nonnegative integer keys and remove cache_outcome and side_effect_class from base metadata.

consequences.security: Strongly content-free but loses useful coarse operational classification.
consequences.compatibility: Drops two ratified base keys.
consequences.schema: Smaller closed metadata object.
consequences.vectors: Categorical keys become schema-invalid.

options.label: Digest categorical values
options.rule: Store only domain-separated digests for cache and side-effect classification.

consequences.security: Content-free if preimages are closed, but opaque digests add no value over enums and complicate audits.
consequences.compatibility: Changes human- and machine-readable activity semantics.
consequences.schema: Two sha256 fields replace enums.
consequences.vectors: Requires a separate closed preimage registry.

recommendation.rationale: It preserves the ratified base keys and existing MCP classifications while closing every content-bearing value channel.

consolidated_resolution_slate.title: Mapping cryptographic collision classification
consolidated_resolution_slate.question: Which exact existing or new error distinguishes a cryptographic mapping collision from an ordinary ownership conflict?

options.label: Narrow existing identity collision
options.rule: Use GKOS_P6_IDENTITY_COLLISION for a generated mapping_id collision or when the same namespace plus subject_digest is presented with a distinct authenticated canonical-subject collision guard/evidence digest. Use GKOS_P6_MAPPING_CONFLICT only for an ordinary existing binding/ownership conflict with no cryptographic mismatch. On collision consume entropy exactly once, perform zero authority mutation, do not overwrite or retry, emit only content-free owner evidence, and treat it as a D0-15 stop-class event.

consequences.security: Cryptographic/entropy failure remains distinguishable from expected uniqueness conflict without leaking the external subject.
consequences.compatibility: Narrows the meaning of an existing owner-only code; no public MCP envelope or code-set expansion.
consequences.counts: Error count remains exactly 53; operations remain 32/24 and tables remain 16.
consequences.schema: external_mapping gains or binds a nonsecret authenticated collision-guard/evidence digest in the existing table; the registry description and exact mapping vectors are corrected.
consequences.vectors: Inject mapping_id and subject-digest collisions; assert one entropy call, IDENTITY_COLLISION, no retry/overwrite/mutation, and distinguish ordinary MAPPING_CONFLICT.

options.label: Add mapping collision code
options.rule: Ratify GKOS_P6_MAPPING_COLLISION as a new owner-only public-registry member with the same no-mutation disposition.

consequences.security: Most explicit name, with equivalent fail-closed behavior.
consequences.compatibility: Changes the closed error registry and every duplicated enum/error fixture.
consequences.counts: Error count becomes 54 and MCP/error vector hashes change.
consequences.schema: All exact 53-code schemas and evidence counts must be amended.
consequences.vectors: Adds a new expected error code across Full/Lite parity.

options.label: Use mapping conflict for both
options.rule: Return GKOS_P6_MAPPING_CONFLICT for ordinary ownership conflicts and cryptographic collisions.

consequences.security: Hides a stop-class entropy/digest anomaly among normal conflicts and cannot prove collision handling.
consequences.compatibility: Preserves the accepted code mapping.
consequences.schema: No new code or narrowed description.
consequences.vectors: Collision and ordinary conflict expected bytes become indistinguishable.

recommendation.rationale: It preserves the closed 53-code registry and gives mapping collision the same stop-class semantics already ratified for identity and credential collisions.

Enforce the one global event union across the four existing event tables: globally unique event_id/global_event_seq, no gaps/forks, exact predecessor, full before/after authority and nullable agent/epoch coordinates, only one bootstrap genesis, exact restore history floor, kind-to-table constants from D015-R08, checked integrity/foreign keys/pragmas, and receipt digests computed only from committed canonical records.

Bind references, sessions, cursors, snapshots, requests, and idempotency to the ratified identity/authority/policy/physical/recovery coordinates; enforce 24-hour idempotency expiry, restore invalidation, process/write-gate invalidation, and startup resealing of every durable record changed to stale/closed.
